definition.criterion: min over azimuth of the in-mesh horizon elevation >= sun_max
definition.empty_bin_handling: excluded from the min (NOT defaulted to -90)

CAVEAT_read_this.problem: the blocked/open split is NOT resolution-independent; it is an artifact of the azimuth binning on a 450-facet mesh
CAVEAT_read_this.why_CC_got_zero: with a fine azimuth grid most facets have empty bins; defaulting an empty bin to -90 deg collapses the min and reports every facet unblocked. My original code had the same fallback and only escaped it because NAZ=36 keeps all bins populated on this mesh.
CAVEAT_read_this.effect_on_the_science: the blocked-minus-all-43 annual-min differential is -0.116 K (NAZ=18) to -0.281 K (NAZ=48); I previously quoted -0.203 K from NAZ=36 alone. Use <=0.3 K as the bound, not 0.20 K.
CAVEAT_read_this.better_basis: the 10 m illumination render shows the PSR70 polygon floor is directly lit 0.00% of the year. At native DEM resolution there is no direct beam on the floor at all, so the blocked/open distinction exists only because the 16x16 mesh under-resolves the rim horizon. Prefer that statement over any in-mesh azimuth horizon.
